readings.title: The instruction nobody wrote
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At Elm Workshop, experienced workers adjusted a machine by listening to its sound. New employees received a written checklist, but it only said 'check operation'. A mentor realised that the checklist omitted the very judgement beginners needed to learn. She recorded examples of normal and unusual sounds and explained when to stop and seek help. Trainees still practised under supervision; the recordings were not permission to diagnose every fault alone. Making hidden knowledge explicit improved the introduction. It also prompted senior staff to discuss differences in their own habits rather than assuming everyone used the same standard.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Questions at the end of the shift
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A supervisor told new staff that they could ask questions at any time. Nevertheless, few did so while the production line was busy. A short discussion at the end of each shift gave them a predictable opportunity. Questions about minor uncertainties increased, and one revealed that two labels were easily confused. The labels were changed before a serious mistake occurred. The supervisor kept the open invitation during work, especially for urgent concerns. The scheduled discussion added a second route; it did not mean that workers should wait until the end of the day to report an immediate risk.

readings.title: A mentor learns to wait
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Tomas was proud of solving problems quickly. When he became a mentor, he often interrupted a trainee's explanation with the answer. The trainee completed tasks but struggled when working alone. Tomas began asking what she had noticed and waiting while she proposed a next step. Progress initially seemed slower, yet he could now see which part of the process she understood. He still intervened immediately when safety required it. For ordinary decisions, however, giving time to think became part of his teaching. Efficiency during one demonstration was not the same as independence after it.

readings.title: The useful handover note
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A maintenance team used long handover messages listing everything completed during a shift. Incoming workers found it difficult to identify unfinished work. The team adopted three short headings: completed, awaiting action and urgent concerns. Details were still available in the main record, but the handover highlighted what the next person needed to do. The new format did not excuse leaving out relevant information. It encouraged writers to consider the reader's next decision. Several workers said preparing the note also helped them notice loose ends before leaving. Writing for someone else improved their own organisation.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

An experienced worker may perform a task so easily that its difficult steps are no longer obvious. Teaching someone else requires those steps to be explained. Questions from a beginner can reveal problems in an established routine. In this way, mentoring can benefit both people.
translation.referenceAnswer: 有经验的员工可能非常轻松地完成一项任务，以至于其中困难的步骤不再显而易见。指导别人就需要把这些步骤解释清楚。初学者的问题能够揭示既有流程中的问题。这样，指导关系就能使双方受益。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Discuss what makes workplace mentoring effective. Include the responsibilities of both an experienced worker and a new colleague.
writing.sampleAnswer: Effective workplace mentoring requires more than showing a new colleague the fastest way to finish a task. An experienced worker should explain the reasons behind important steps, invite questions and make safety limits clear. The learner should practise actively, describe uncertainties and ask for help before taking an unfamiliar risk. For example, a mentor could demonstrate a machine check, then ask the learner to explain what they notice while repeating it under supervision. Regular short discussions can reveal misunderstandings before they become habits. Mentors should also be willing to learn from a beginner's questions. A good relationship develops independence gradually, while ensuring that speed and confidence never become substitutes for understanding.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
